disputed: This synthesis connects documented facts into a pattern. The $190 billion ROI figure comes from a partisan minority report with its own methodology. The administration's position is that 'energy dominance' lowers costs and strengthens national security, and that the industry supports it because the policy is good for the industry, not because the policy was bought. No court or inspector general has found an explicit quid pro quo. Readers should weigh the pattern against that lack of direct proof.

items: Money: $201 million in fossil-fuel donations to the reelection effort and $19 million to the inauguration, after an explicit $1 billion ask.
Personnel: Energy (Wright), Interior (Burgum, close to Hamm), 26 senior officials from polluting industries, and an ex-Exxon lawyer at DOJ.
Law: OBBBA royalty cuts, mandated lease sales, the delayed methane fee, and about $18 billion in tax incentives.
Regulation: the Endangerment Finding repeal, built on an illegally run DOE advisory group, plus more than 125 climate rollbacks.
Competition: offshore wind halted, more than 160 wind projects frozen, and coal plants kept running at ratepayers' expense.
Enforcement and courts: polluter lawsuits down 76-81%, and DOJ suing states to protect oil companies from climate liability.

Foreign policy: oil-industry briefings before the Venezuela strikes, US-controlled Venezuelan oil revenue, a 100-year oil concession, energy-purchase commitments inside tariff deals, and war-driven windfall profits.

The Senate Democratic report estimates a $190 billion return for fossil-fuel donors. (Senate EPW Democrats (https://www.epw.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/press-releases-democratic?ID=D17E87C8-BA5B-4D3A-BA7A-CAD03C4B6F2D))
sections.label: The chain

items: The July 2025 US-EU tariff deal included an EU commitment to buy $750 billion in US energy over three years, a figure analysts called unlikely to materialize. It shows US LNG and oil sales being built into tariff negotiations. (CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2025/07/29/trump-eu-trade-deal-energy-gas-oil-lng-nuclear.html))
sections.label: Trade deals as energy sales

summary: Taken together, these items show a pattern that runs through the whole administration, not only Trump personally: industry money came in (the $1 billion ask), industry people were put in charge (Wright, Burgum, EPA and DOJ appointees), and then law, regulation, enforcement, litigation and foreign policy all moved in the industry's favor.
title: Synthesis: Big Oil's return on investment across the whole administration
